options.text: A reaction where two elements combine to form a compound
A reaction where a more reactive element takes the place of a less reactive element in a compound
A reaction where a compound breaks down into simpler substances
A reaction where two compounds swap their elements

questions.explanation: In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces (pushes out) a less reactive element from its compound. The more reactive element 'wins' the place in the compound.

questions.stem: Will zinc displace copper from copper sulfate solution?

options.text: No, because copper is more reactive than zinc
No, because they are equally reactive
Yes, because zinc is more reactive than copper
Yes, because copper sulfate is a strong acid

questions.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than copper in the reactivity series. Therefore, zinc can displace copper from copper sulfate solution: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. The blue solution would become colourless and copper metal would appear.

questions.stem: What would you observe if iron is placed in copper sulfate solution?

options.text: Nothing happens
The solution turns from blue to pale green and a brown-orange solid appears on the iron
The solution turns red
Bubbles of gas are produced

questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper. The blue colour of copper sulfate fades as it becomes iron(II) sulfate (pale green), and copper metal deposits as a brown-orange coating on the iron.

questions.stem: Which of the following displacement reactions would NOT occur?

options.text: Zinc + copper sulfate solution
Magnesium + zinc chloride solution
Copper + silver nitrate solution
Copper + magnesium sulfate solution

questions.explanation: Copper cannot displace magnesium because copper is less reactive than magnesium. A less reactive metal cannot displace a more reactive metal from its compound. The other reactions would all occur because the added metal is more reactive.

questions.stem: In the displacement reaction Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu, which substance is oxidised?

options.text: Copper sulfate
Zinc sulfate
Zinc
Copper

questions.explanation: Zinc is oxidised because it loses electrons: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻. The copper ions are reduced because they gain electrons: Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. This is a redox reaction.

questions.stem: Displacement reactions can also occur between metals and metal oxides. What happens when magnesium is heated with copper oxide?

options.text: Nothing happens because they are both metals
Magnesium displaces copper, forming magnesium oxide and copper
Copper displaces magnesium, forming copper oxide and magnesium
Both metals dissolve

questions.explanation: Magnesium is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper oxide: Mg + CuO → MgO + Cu. The magnesium is oxidised (gains oxygen) and the copper oxide is reduced (loses oxygen).

questions.stem: A student adds a piece of metal X to a solution of metal Y sulfate. No reaction occurs. What can be concluded?

options.text: Metal X is more reactive than metal Y
Metal X and metal Y are equally reactive
Metal X is less reactive than metal Y
The solution was too dilute

questions.explanation: If no displacement occurs, it means metal X cannot push metal Y out of its compound. This tells us metal X is less reactive than metal Y, as only a more reactive metal can displace a less reactive one.
